# @rebar-ui/placement

The recommended way to build with rebar-ui: compose a `Block[]` document (a fixed vocabulary of
named archetypes) and render it through `BlockRenderer`, instead of hand-authoring `Stack`/`Box`/
`Card` JSX against `rebar-ui` directly — measured cheaper, faster, and far more consistent. See
`README.md` for the full archetype list and per-harness prompt guidance (agentic vs.
single-completion-call, and image-driven tasks specifically). Read `dist/index.d.ts` for exact
current TypeScript shapes, not `src/`.

`BlockRenderer` already renders the correct page root (a plain wrapper on top of the page's own
already-correct background) — render its output directly as the page, never nested inside a
`Card` or other bounded/backgrounded element "for structure." That wraps the whole page in one
component's border/shadow/padding, producing a page that looks like a single giant grey/boxed
rectangle instead of a normal page with individual cards on it.
